title: Additive restriction of conductor tensor sections
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] whose underlying space is the union of finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, each given its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\subset Y$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on $Z_2\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $\mathcal I_1$ be the image of $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}$ in $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$. For any invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and any $m\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal I\mathcal M^{\otimes m})\cong\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal I_1(\mathcal M|_{Z_1})^{\otimes m})$. More precisely the additive restriction map between the tensor products of the ideal modules and the invertible tensor powers is bijective, and commutes with the two inclusions into the ambient tensor powers. No claim about extensions as ambient sections or their nonvanishing loci is included.

source.place: Varieties Remark 09NW and Lemma 09NX, displayed conductor equality

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-conductor-ideal-zero-intersection] to the reduced component cover. It supplies a bijection on sections of the image sheaves of the two ideal multiplication maps, commuting with restriction.

Identify the image of the adjoint map from the pulled-back complementary ideal with the module associated to the comap ideal. On affine opens this is the ideal generated by the images of the original ideal, and both constructions glue with their inclusions. The ideal restriction result [lem-sc-conductor-ideal-restriction] identifies the pulled-back ideal with this image. Tensor powers of invertible modules are invertible and pullback commutes with tensor powers. Hence the two tensor multiplication maps are monomorphisms, and their maps to their categorical images are isomorphisms. Transport the section bijection through these isomorphisms.

Compare the adjunction chosen in the conductor lemmas with the canonical tensor-pullback adjunction. The comparison is a natural automorphism of pullback, and takes one unit to the other. Its linear automorphism on the pulled-back tensor power preserves the product with the extended ideal. Compose the section bijection with this comparison and with the tensor-power identification; the commutative square from the conductor lemma becomes precisely the displayed compatibility with the canonical restriction map. The additive map is bijective since every comparison used is an isomorphism.
